title: Wet Lungs, Clots and Collapsed Lungs: PCP Decisions

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already sit heart-failure patients up with legs down, give oxygen, and bag them when breathing fails. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Tell pneumonia from pulmonary edema, and why it matters
  2. Recognize PE, pneumothorax, effusion and hyperventilation
  3. Apply BC's CHF protocol: CPAP, PEEP, and what not to give

Textbook: Chapter 29, PDF pages 2486–2521
slides.say: Welcome to the last lesson of Chapter twenty-nine. Last time we treated airways that squeeze shut. Today the problem is deeper: alveoli full of pus or fluid, blood that can't reach the lungs, air or fluid around the lung, and breathing that's too fast or too slow. As EMRs you already sit heart-failure patients up with their legs down, give oxygen, and bag when breathing fails. As a PCP, you add CPAP and PEEP, and you must decide when they help and when they harm. Today: pneumonia versus pulmonary edema; PE, pneumothorax, effusion and hyperventilation; and the BC heart-failure protocol.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第二十九章最后一课。上节课处理的是会收缩关闭的气道，今天的问题更深一层：肺泡里充满脓或液体、血流到不了肺、肺周围有气或有液，以及呼吸太快或太慢。作为 EMR，你们已经会让心衰病人坐起、双腿下垂、给氧，呼吸衰竭时用球囊面罩通气。作为 PCP，你多了 CPAP 和 PEEP，也必须判断它们什么时候有帮助、什么时候有害。今天讲：肺炎和肺水肿的区别；肺栓塞、气胸、胸腔积液和过度通气；以及 BC 的心衰流程。

slides.title: Where the oxygen gets lost
slides.body:
UnitAirBloodExample
Normalyesyeshealthy lung
Dead spaceyesnopulmonary embolism, shock
Shuntnoyespneumonia, edema, collapse
Silentnonocardiac arrest

Reopening alveoli helps shunt; dead space needs blood flow back.
slides.say: One idea ties today's diseases together. Gas exchange needs two things in the same place: air in the alveoli, and blood in the capillaries next to them. When air arrives but blood doesn't, that's dead space, as in a pulmonary embolism or shock. When blood arrives but the alveoli are full of pus or fluid, or collapsed, that's shunt, as in pneumonia, pulmonary edema or atelectasis. When neither arrives, as in cardiac arrest, the unit is silent. Why should a PCP care? Because the fix differs. Shunt can improve when you reopen the alveoli, which is how CPAP works. Dead space needs blood flow restored, which only the hospital can do.
slides.sayZh: 有一个概念能把今天的疾病串起来。气体交换需要两样东西在同一处：肺泡里有气，旁边毛细血管里有血。有气没血叫无效腔，比如肺栓塞或休克。有血没气，就是肺泡被脓或液体填满、或者塌陷，叫分流，比如肺炎、肺水肿或肺不张。两样都没有，比如心搏骤停，叫静默单位。PCP 为什么要懂这个？因为处理不同。分流可以通过重新撑开肺泡来改善，这正是 CPAP 的原理；无效腔需要恢复血流，只有医院能做到。

slides.title: Pneumonia
slides.body:
• Often after the flu; elderly, smokers, chronic illness, bedridden
  • Fever, chills, productive cough, chest pain worse on coughing
  • Crackles, usually at one base; later quiet over consolidation
  • Often dehydrated: thick sputum, dry mouth
  • Bronchodilators don't treat it; may help if asthma/COPD too

Over 6,000 Canadians die of pneumonia each year.
slides.say: Pneumonia is an infection that fills alveoli with pus. Over six thousand Canadians die of it every year. It often follows the flu, so listen for "I just got over the flu last week." Older people, smokers, the chronically ill, the bedridden, and anyone who can't clear secretions are at risk. The patient usually has hours to days of weakness, fever or shaking chills, a productive cough, and chest pain that's worse on coughing. Listen for crackles, usually at one base; in advanced cases the area over the consolidation goes quiet. Many patients are dehydrated. A bronchodilator won't treat the pneumonia, but it may help a little if the patient also has asthma or COPD.
slides.sayZh: 肺炎是肺泡被脓填满的感染。加拿大每年有六千多人死于肺炎。它常继发于流感，所以留意病人说「我上周刚得过流感」。老人、吸烟者、慢性病人、卧床者，以及任何排痰困难的人都是高危人群。病人通常有几小时到几天的乏力、发热或寒战、咳痰，以及咳嗽时加重的胸痛。听诊常在一侧肺底听到湿啰音；病情进展后，实变的区域会变安静。很多病人有脱水。支气管扩张剂治不了肺炎，但如果病人同时有哮喘或 COPD，可能有一点帮助。

slides.title: Pulmonary edema: a rising tide
slides.body:
Earlyfine crackles at the basesend of inspiration; listen on the back
Worsecrackles rise to the shoulder bladesthen to the apices
Severecoarse crackles, in and outpink, frothy sputum

Most common cause: left heart failure after an MI. Also toxins (even 24 h later), infection, altitude.
slides.say: In pulmonary edema, fluid from the blood leaks into the lung tissue, and later into the alveoli. Gas exchange suffers long before you see froth. The most common cause is left heart failure after a heart attack, but inhaled toxins, infection, trauma and altitude can do it too; some toxic gases cause edema up to twenty-four hours after exposure. Think of it as a rising tide. Early, you hear fine crackles at the bases at the end of each breath in, so always listen on the back. As it worsens, the crackles climb to the shoulder blades, then to the apices. In severe cases you hear coarse crackles on both phases, and the patient coughs up pink, frothy sputum.
slides.sayZh: 肺水肿是血液里的液体渗进肺组织，之后进入肺泡。在你看到泡沫之前，气体交换早已受损。最常见的原因是心梗后的左心衰，但吸入毒物、感染、创伤和高原也会导致；有些毒气在接触后长达二十四小时才引起肺水肿。把它想成涨潮：早期在肺底吸气末听到细湿啰音，所以一定要听背部；加重后啰音升到肩胛骨水平，再到肺尖；重度时吸气、呼气都有粗湿啰音，病人咳粉红色泡沫痰。

slides.title: Pneumonia or pulmonary edema?
slides.body:
PneumoniaPulmonary edema
Onsethours to days, after fluoften sudden; PND
Feveryes, chillsusually not
Cracklesoften one baseboth bases, rising
Sputumthick or purulentfrothy, pink
OtherdehydratedJVD, leg edema, heart history

Why it matters: fluid can help one and drown the other.
slides.say: Both conditions give you crackles, so how do you tell them apart? Look at the whole picture. Pneumonia usually builds over hours to days, often after the flu, with fever, chills, and thick or pus-like sputum. The crackles are often at one base, and the patient may be dry. Pulmonary edema is often sudden, sometimes waking the patient at night. There's usually no fever. The crackles are in both bases and climbing, the sputum is frothy and pink, and you may find distended neck veins, swollen legs and a cardiac history. Why does this matter so much now? Because as a PCP you control fluids and pressure, and the wrong choice can drown a patient with edema.
slides.sayZh: 两种病都能听到湿啰音，怎么区分？看整体。肺炎通常几小时到几天内逐渐加重，常在流感之后，伴发热、寒战，痰稠或呈脓性；啰音常在一侧肺底，病人可能偏干。肺水肿常突然发生，有时让病人夜里憋醒，通常不发热；啰音在两侧肺底并不断上升，痰是粉红色泡沫样，还可能有颈静脉怒张、腿肿和心脏病史。为什么现在这点这么重要？因为作为 PCP，你掌控着补液和正压，选错了可能把肺水肿病人「淹死」。

slides.q: An 80-year-old has felt unwell for three days since having the flu. Which finding points most to pneumonia rather than pulmonary edema?
options: Crackles rising in both lungs to the shoulder blades
Fever, thick yellow-green sputum, crackles at one base
Woke at 3 a.m. gasping and must sleep sitting up
Distended neck veins and swollen ankles
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. An eighty-year-old has felt unwell for three days since having the flu. Which finding points most to pneumonia rather than pulmonary edema? A, crackles rising in both lungs to the shoulder blades. B, fever, thick yellow-green sputum, and crackles at one base. C, woke at three in the morning gasping and must sleep sitting up. D, distended neck veins and swollen ankles. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位八十岁老人得流感后不舒服了三天。下面哪项最支持肺炎而不是肺水肿？A 两肺湿啰音上升到肩胛骨水平；B 发热、黄绿色稠痰、一侧肺底湿啰音；C 凌晨三点憋醒，必须坐着睡；D 颈静脉怒张、脚踝水肿。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Fever, coloured sputum and crackles on one side fit an infection, especially after the flu. A describes the rising crackles of pulmonary edema. C is paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea and orthopnea, which point to heart failure. D suggests fluid overload and right heart failure. Older patients can have both problems, so put the whole picture together before you choose fluids or pressure.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。发热、有颜色的痰、单侧湿啰音符合感染，尤其在流感之后。A 是肺水肿那种不断上升的湿啰音。C 是夜间阵发性呼吸困难和端坐呼吸，指向心衰。D 提示液体过多和右心衰。老年人可能两者兼有，所以决定补液或正压之前要把整体情况拼起来。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: CHF / pulmonary edema
slides.body:
BC protocol: CHF or pulmonary edema (also drowning, cardiogenic shock, toxin exposure)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Rest; bring the equipment to the patient
  • Sit upright, legs hanging down; keep warm
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if LOC altered or SpO₂ < 94%
  • Transport

PCP adds (on scene)

  • Consider CPAP
  • BVM needed: consider a PEEP valve, 5 cmH₂O to start
  • BC's CPAP guideline also lists pneumonia
slides.say: Here's the BC protocol for heart failure and pulmonary edema; it also covers drowning, cardiogenic shock and toxic exposure. The left column is familiar: keep the patient at rest, and bring the stretcher and lifting devices to them instead of letting them walk. Sit them upright with the legs hanging down, keep them warm, give oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, assist ventilations if consciousness drops or the saturation stays low, and transport. The right column is yours: on scene, consider CPAP, and if you need to bag, consider a PEEP valve starting at five. You practised both step by step in Chapters thirteen and fourteen. Note that BC's CPAP guideline also lists pneumonia.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的心衰和肺水肿流程，也适用于溺水、心源性休克和毒物暴露。左栏很熟悉：让病人保持休息，把担架和搬运设备带到病人身边，不让他走路；坐直、双腿下垂、保暖；给氧使血氧达到百分之九十四以上；意识下降或血氧仍低就辅助通气；转运。右栏是你的：在现场考虑 CPAP；需要捏球时，考虑加 PEEP 阀，从五开始。这两样在第十三、十四章已经一步步练过。注意，BC 的 CPAP 指南也把肺炎列为适应证。

slides.title: Fluids: a double-edged tool
slides.body:
• Book: young and dehydrated (pneumonia, asthma) → fluid helps
  • Elderly or weak heart: fluid can cause pulmonary edema
  • Listen to the lungs before and after any fluid
  • Not all crackles are edema: diuretics worsen pneumonia
  • BC's SOB and CHF protocols list no IV fluids
  • Where BC calls for a bolus: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
slides.say: As an EMR, fluids were never your problem. Now they are. The textbook says that dehydrated young patients with pneumonia or asthma often get a fluid bolus. But in an older patient, or anyone with a weak heart, too much fluid can push them into pulmonary edema. So listen to the lungs before and after any fluid. The same logic works in reverse: not every crackle is edema, and the book warns that diuretics make pneumonia and asthma worse. Now the BC rules. The BC shortness-of-breath and heart-failure protocols don't list IV fluids. Where a BC protocol does call for a bolus, it's twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred.
slides.sayZh: 当 EMR 时，补液从来不是你的事，现在是了。教材说，脱水的年轻肺炎或哮喘病人常会给一次补液推注。但对老人或心脏功能差的人，液体给多了会把他推进肺水肿。所以任何补液前后都要听肺。反过来也一样：不是每个湿啰音都是肺水肿，书里提醒利尿剂会让肺炎和哮喘更糟。再看 BC 规定：BC 的气短流程和心衰流程都没有列静脉补液。凡是 BC 流程要求推注补液的，都是每公斤二十毫升、最多两升、每五百毫升复评一次。

slides.title: Pneumothorax and pleural effusion
slides.body:
Whotall, thin smokers; COPD; severe asthmaweak spots called blebs
Storysharp pain after a cough, then breathlessor after forceful BVM
Effusionfluid around the lung; quiet soundskeep them sitting up

Pneumothorax: high-flow O₂, monitor, transport. In BC: no CPAP; needle decompression is outside EMR/PCP scope.
slides.say: Now the space around the lung. In a pneumothorax, air collects between the two layers of pleura. Weak spots called blebs can burst with a simple cough, or with forceful bagging. They're common in tall, thin people, especially smokers, and in COPD and severe asthma. The typical story is a sharp pain after a cough, then breathlessness that grows over minutes to hours. Give high-flow oxygen, monitor closely, and transport. In BC, a suspected pneumothorax rules out CPAP, and needle decompression is outside EMR and PCP scope. A pleural effusion is fluid around the lung, sometimes litres of it. Breath sounds are hard to hear, and the patient will fight to stay sitting up. Let them.
slides.sayZh: 再看肺的外面。气胸是空气积在两层胸膜之间。肺上叫肺大疱的薄弱点，咳一声或用力捏球都可能破。高瘦的人，尤其吸烟者，以及 COPD 和重度哮喘病人多见。典型经过是咳嗽后一阵锐痛，然后几分钟到几小时内越来越喘。给高流量氧，密切监测，转运。在 BC，怀疑气胸就不能用 CPAP，针刺减压也不在 EMR 和 PCP 的范围内。胸腔积液是肺周围积液，有时多达几升。呼吸音很难听到，病人会拼命保持坐位，就让他坐着。

slides.q: A tall, thin 22-year-old smoker felt a sharp chest pain after coughing. RR 26, SpO₂ 91% on O₂, quieter sounds on the left, BP 118/76, alert. Your partner reaches for CPAP. Best plan?
options: CPAP at 5 cmH₂O, stepping up by 2.5 if needed
No CPAP: high-flow O₂, position of comfort, watch for tension, transport
Needle decompression of the left chest
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A tall, thin twenty-two-year-old smoker felt a sharp chest pain after coughing. His rate is twenty-six, his saturation ninety-one percent on oxygen, breath sounds are quieter on the left, his blood pressure is one hundred eighteen over seventy-six, and he's alert. Your partner reaches for CPAP. What's the best plan? A, CPAP at five centimetres of water, stepping up by two point five if needed. B, no CPAP: high-flow oxygen, position of comfort, watch for tension, and transport. C, needle decompression of the left chest. D, salbutamol five milligrams by nebulizer first. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位高瘦的二十二岁吸烟男性咳嗽后突发胸部锐痛。呼吸二十六次，吸氧下血氧百分之九十一，左侧呼吸音减弱，血压一百一十八比七十六，神志清楚。你的搭档伸手去拿 CPAP。最好的方案是什么？A 以五厘米水柱启动 CPAP，需要时每次加二点五；B 不用 CPAP：高流量氧、舒适体位、警惕张力性气胸、转运；C 左胸针刺减压；D 先雾化五毫克沙丁胺醇。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Sudden sharp pain after a cough in a tall, thin smoker, with one quiet side, suggests a spontaneous pneumothorax. A suspected pneumothorax is a BC contraindication to CPAP, because positive pressure can turn it into a tension pneumothorax. C is outside EMR and PCP scope in BC. D treats bronchospasm, which isn't his problem.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。高瘦吸烟者咳嗽后突发锐痛、一侧呼吸音减弱，提示自发性气胸。怀疑气胸是 BC 规定的 CPAP 禁忌证，因为正压可能把它变成张力性气胸。C 在 BC 不属于 EMR 和 PCP 的范围。D 治的是支气管痉挛，而他的问题不是这个。

slides.title: Pulmonary embolism
slides.body:
Sudden breathlessness ± sharp chest pain: think PE

  • Usually a DVT from the legs: swollen, tender calf
  • Risks: surgery, immobility, long trips, pregnancy, the pill, cancer
  • Often nothing obvious in the lungs
  • Huge clot: shock or arrest; few survive

Other emboli: fat (fractures), amniotic fluid, air (neck wound, unflushed IV line).
slides.say: A pulmonary embolism, or PE, is one of the most often missed diagnoses in emergency medicine, because nothing obviously looks wrong with the lungs. Think of it whenever someone has sudden shortness of breath, with or without a sharp chest pain. Most clots start as a deep vein thrombosis in the legs, so look for a swollen, tender calf. Risk factors include recent surgery, immobility, long car or plane trips, pregnancy, birth-control pills and some cancers, but many patients have none. A huge clot at the split of the pulmonary arteries can cause shock or cardiac arrest, and few survive. Other things can embolize too, including air from an IV line that wasn't flushed.
slides.sayZh: 肺栓塞是急诊医学里最常被漏诊的病之一，因为肺看起来没什么明显异常。只要有人突然气短，伴或不伴胸部锐痛，就要想到它。大多数血栓来自腿部的深静脉血栓，所以看有没有小腿肿胀、压痛。危险因素包括近期手术、长期不动、长途开车或坐飞机、怀孕、口服避孕药和某些癌症，但很多病人一个都没有。卡在肺动脉分叉处的巨大血栓可导致休克或心搏骤停，很少有人能活下来。别的东西也会造成栓塞，包括没冲管的输液器里的空气。

slides.title: Breathing too much or too little
slides.body:
Too muchToo little
CO₂falls → alkalosisrises → acidosis
Signstingling hands, feet, mouth; panicslow, shallow, drowsy
EMS causestress, but rule out the restopioid overdose (most common)
Docalm coaching; no paper bagBVM first, then naloxone

Normal: about 500 mL × 12–16/min = 6–8 L/min; PaCO₂ 35–45 mmHg.
slides.say: Ventilation is judged by carbon dioxide, not oxygen. At rest, about five hundred millilitres, twelve to sixteen times a minute, keeps the carbon dioxide between thirty-five and forty-five. Breathe too much, and carbon dioxide falls: tingling in the hands, feet and around the mouth, and a feeling of not getting enough air. Never use a paper bag; it can make the patient hypoxic, and a patient breathing fast to blow off acid, as in ketoacidosis or a poisoning, can be badly harmed. Coach calmly instead. Breathe too little, and carbon dioxide rises. In EMS, the most common cause is an opioid overdose: ventilate with a BVM first, then give naloxone.
slides.sayZh: 判断通气看二氧化碳，不看氧。静息时每次约五百毫升、每分钟十二到十六次，能把二氧化碳维持在三十五到四十五。呼吸过度，二氧化碳下降：手脚和口周发麻，还觉得吸不够气。绝不要用纸袋：它可能让病人缺氧，而靠深快呼吸排酸的病人，比如酮症酸中毒或中毒，会被严重伤害。改用平静的引导。呼吸过少，二氧化碳上升。急救中最常见的原因是阿片类过量：先用球囊面罩通气，再给纳洛酮。

slides.title: Any breathless patient: the PCP plan
slides.body:
1. Clear the mouth, suction, position of comfort
  2. Cut the work: loosen clothing, sit up, don't let them walk
  3. O₂: NRB if breathing well; BVM if not
  4. Bronchodilator only for spasm; otherwise the NRB wins
  5. Tiring but awake? Consider CPAP; agitation means fix the O₂
  6. Reassess breath sounds and SpO₂ after every step
slides.say: Let's pull it together into a plan for any breathless patient. First the airway: clear out food or gum, suction, and let the patient find the most comfortable position. Then cut the work of breathing: loosen tight clothing, help them sit up, and never let them walk. Give oxygen by non-rebreather if they're breathing well, and by BVM if they're not. Use a bronchodilator when there's spasm; without spasm, a nebulizer can actually give less oxygen than the non-rebreather. If the patient is tiring but still awake, consider CPAP. If they're agitated, fix their oxygen and ventilation; don't reach for sedation. And after every step, listen again and recheck the saturation.
slides.sayZh: 把它整理成一套适用于任何气短病人的方案。先管气道：清出食物或口香糖，吸引，让病人找到最舒服的体位。再减轻呼吸做功：松开紧身衣物，扶他坐起，绝不让他走路。呼吸够的用非重复呼吸面罩给氧，不够的用球囊面罩。有痉挛才用支气管扩张剂；没有痉挛时，雾化给的氧反而比非重复呼吸面罩少。病人累了但还清醒，考虑 CPAP。病人烦躁时，要纠正氧合和通气，而不是想着镇静。每一步之后，都要重新听诊、复查血氧。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• CPAP: not with pneumothorax, SBP < 90, low LOC, vomiting
  • Pressure can turn a simple pneumothorax into a tension one
  • Fluid with an old or weak heart: listen to the lungs often
  • Crackles aren't always edema: check fever, sputum, history
  • Prime and flush IV tubing: air in the line can embolize
  • Never call it "just hyperventilation": check glucose, think toxins
slides.say: Now the new risks. CPAP is not for a suspected pneumothorax, a systolic under ninety, a falling level of consciousness, or vomiting. Even when you start it correctly, positive pressure can turn a simple pneumothorax into a tension pneumothorax, so keep listening to both sides. If you give fluid to an older patient or one with a weak heart, listen to the lungs often. Crackles aren't always edema, so check for fever, sputum changes and the history before you decide. When you start an IV, prime and flush the tubing, because air in the line can cause an air embolism. And never settle on "just hyperventilation" until you've checked the glucose and thought about toxins.
slides.sayZh: 现在说新的风险。CPAP 不能用于疑似气胸、收缩压低于九十、意识下降或呕吐的病人。即使启动得完全正确，正压也可能把单纯气胸变成张力性气胸，所以要持续听两侧。给老人或心功能差的人补液时，要经常听肺。湿啰音不一定是肺水肿，下结论前先查发热、痰的变化和病史。开静脉时要排气、冲管，因为管路里的空气会造成空气栓塞。在测过血糖、想过中毒之前，绝不要轻易断定「只是过度通气」。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: furosemide, nitro, morphine for edema: not in BC's CHF protocol
  • BC nitroglycerin is for cardiac chest pain only
  • Book: needle decompression. BC: outside EMR/PCP scope
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV q 3 min, or 4 mg IN
  • PCP adds IV naloxone if still unconscious and apneic

Pulmonary thrombosis and tension pneumothorax are BC reversible arrest causes where transport can be considered.
slides.say: A few BC points. The textbook treats pulmonary edema with furosemide, nitroglycerin and morphine. None of these is in the BC heart-failure protocol. Furosemide and morphine aren't BC exam drugs at all, and BC's nitroglycerin is for cardiac chest pain. The book mentions needle decompression for a pneumothorax; in BC that's outside EMR and PCP scope. The book says to titrate naloxone to breathing; BC gives zero point four milligrams, then zero point four, zero point eight and two milligrams, IM or IV, every three minutes, or four milligrams intranasally, after ventilating. The PCP may give it IV if the patient stays unconscious and apneic. And in arrest, BC lists pulmonary thrombosis and tension pneumothorax as reversible causes where transport can be considered.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考点。教材用呋塞米、硝酸甘油和吗啡治疗肺水肿，这些都不在 BC 心衰流程里；呋塞米和吗啡根本不是 BC 考纲药物，BC 的硝酸甘油只用于心源性胸痛。书里提到气胸针刺减压，在 BC 不属于 EMR 和 PCP 的范围。书里说纳洛酮滴定到呼吸改善；BC 是先保证通气，再给零点四毫克，然后零点四、零点八、二毫克，肌注或静注，每三分钟评估，或者鼻喷四毫克。病人持续昏迷、无呼吸时，PCP 可以静脉给药。心搏骤停时，BC 把肺血栓和张力性气胸列为可逆原因，可以考虑转运。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Pneumonia: fever, one base. Edema: sudden, PND, rising crackles
  2. BC CHF: sit up, O₂; PCP adds CPAP or BVM + PEEP
  3. Sudden, lungs unremarkable: PE. One quiet side: pneumothorax, no CPAP

Next: Chapter 30, Cardiovascular Emergencies
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: pneumonia usually brings fever, coloured sputum and crackles at one base; pulmonary edema is often sudden, wakes people at night, and its crackles rise from both bases. Two: in the BC heart-failure protocol, everyone sits the patient up and gives oxygen; the PCP adds CPAP, or a PEEP valve when bagging, and no drugs. Three: sudden breathlessness with lungs that sound unremarkable should make you think of a pulmonary embolism, and one quiet side after a cough suggests a pneumothorax, so no CPAP. Next chapter: cardiovascular emergencies, where heart failure comes back from the heart's side. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，肺炎通常有发热、有颜色的痰和一侧肺底湿啰音；肺水肿常突然发生、夜里憋醒，湿啰音从两侧肺底往上升。二，在 BC 心衰流程中，所有人都让病人坐起、给氧；PCP 加上 CPAP，或捏球时加 PEEP 阀，不用药物。三，突然气短而肺部听起来没什么异常，要想到肺栓塞；咳嗽后一侧呼吸音减弱提示气胸，不能用 CPAP。下一章是心血管急症，我们会从心脏这一侧再讲心衰。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
